questions.stem:
Consider the relation $R$ on the set $\{-2, -1, 0, 1, 2\}$ defined by $(a, b)$ in $\in R$ if and only if $1 + ab > 0$. Then, among the statements:
I. The number of elements in $R$ is 17
II. $R$ is an equivalence relation
questions.solution:
$(a, a) \in R$ because $1 + a^{2} > 0$
$\therefore$ Reflexive
If $1 + ab > 0 \Rightarrow 1 + ba > 0$
$\therefore (a, b) \in R$ and $(b, a) \in R$
$(-2, 0) \in R (0, 1) \in R$
But $(-2, 1) \notin R$
Hence it is not transitive
$\therefore$ It is not equivalence
Total number of elements in the relation $R$ is 17
Because Total elements $= 25$
But $(-2, 1)(-2, 2)(-1, 2)(1, -2)(2, -2)(2, -1)$
$(-1, 1)$ and $(1, -1)$ are not in relation.

options.text: Both I and II are true
Neither I nor II is true

questions.stem:
If the system of linear equations:
$x + y + z = 6$,
$x + 2y + 5z = 10$,
$2x + 3y + \lambda z = \mu$
has infinitely many solutions, then the value of $\lambda + \mu$ equals:
questions.solution:
for Infinite Many-solution
$\Delta = 0$ and $\Delta_1 = \Delta_2 = \Delta_3 = 0$
$\Delta = \begin{vmatrix} 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & 5 \\ 2 & 3 & \lambda \end{vmatrix} = 0$
$(2\lambda - 15) - (\lambda - 10) + (-1) = 0$
$\lambda = 6$
Sum of equation 1 and 2
$2x + 3y + 6z = 16$
equation (3) is $2x + 3y + 6z = \mu$
for $\infty$ many So $\mu = 16$
$\therefore \lambda + \mu = 6 + 16$
$= 22$

questions.stem: Let $A = \begin{bmatrix} \alpha & 1 & 2 \\ 2 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 5 \end{bmatrix}$ and $B = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -5\alpha & 0 \\ 0 & 4\alpha & -2\alpha \end{bmatrix} + \mathrm{adj}(A)$. If $\det(B) = 66$, then $\det(\mathrm{adj}(A))$ equals :
questions.solution:
$A = \begin{bmatrix} \alpha & 1 & 2 \\ 2 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 5 \end{bmatrix}$
$\mathrm{adj}(A) = \begin{bmatrix} 15 & 3 & -6 \\ -10 & 5\alpha & 4 \\ 8 & -4\alpha & 3\alpha - 2 \end{bmatrix}$
Now $B = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -5\alpha & 0 \\ 0 & 4\alpha & -2\alpha \end{bmatrix} + \begin{bmatrix} 15 & 3 & -6 \\ -10 & 5\alpha & 4 \\ 8 & -4\alpha & 3\alpha - 2 \end{bmatrix}$
$= \begin{bmatrix} 16 & 3 & -6 \\ -10 & 0 & 4 \\ 8 & 0 & \alpha - 2 \end{bmatrix}$
As $|B| = 66 \quad \therefore \alpha = 1$
Now $|\mathrm{adj}\,A| = |A|^{n-1} = |A|^{2}$
$|A| = \begin{vmatrix} 1 & 1 & 2 \\ 2 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 5 \end{vmatrix} = 21$
$\therefore |\mathrm{adj}\,A| = 21^{2} = 441$

questions.stem: Let $\alpha = 3 + 4 + 8 + 9 + 13 + 14 + \ldots$ upto 40 terms. If $(\tan\beta)^{\frac{\alpha}{1020}}$ is a root of the equation $x^{2} + x - 2 = 0$, $\beta \in \left(0, \frac{\pi}{2}\right)$ then $\sin^{2}\beta + 3\cos^{2}\beta$ is equal to :
questions.solution:
$\alpha = (3 + 8 + 13 \ldots$ upto 20 terms$) + (4 + 9 + 14 + \ldots$ upto 20 terms$)$
$= \frac{20}{2}[6 + 19 \times 5] + \frac{20}{2}(8 + 19 \times 5) = 2040$
$(\tan\beta)^{\frac{2040}{1020}} = \tan^{2}\beta$
Now, roots of $x^{2} + x - 2 = 0$
$x^{2} + 2x - x - 2 = 0$
$x(x + 2) - (x + 2) = 0$
$\Rightarrow x = -2, 1$
$\Rightarrow \tan^{2}\beta = 1$
$\beta = \frac{\pi}{4}$
$\therefore \sin^{2}\frac{\pi}{4} + 3\cos^{2}\frac{\pi}{4}$
$\frac{1}{2} + \frac{3}{2} \Rightarrow 2$

questions.stem: A candidate has to go to the examination centre to appear in an examination. The candidate uses only one means of transportation for the entire distance out of bus, scooter and car. The probabilities of the candidate going by bus, scooter and car, respectively, are $\frac{2}{5}, \frac{1}{5}$ and $\frac{2}{5}$. The probabilities that the candidate reaches late at the examination centre are $\frac{1}{5}, \frac{1}{3}$ and $\frac{1}{4}$ if the candidate uses bus, scooter and car, respectively. Given that the candidate reached late at the examination centre, the probability that the candidate travelled by bus is:
questions.solution:
Prob of being late
$P(L) = \left(\frac{2}{5} \times \frac{1}{5}\right) + \left(\frac{1}{5} \times \frac{1}{3}\right) + \left(\frac{2}{5} \times \frac{1}{4}\right)$
$= \frac{2}{25} + \frac{1}{15} + \frac{2}{20} = \frac{37}{150}$
$P(\text{Requiral}) = \frac{\frac{2}{25}}{\frac{37}{150}} = \frac{12}{37}$

Let $\alpha = 3\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{6}{11}\right)$ and $\beta = 3\cos^{-1}\left(\frac{4}{9}\right)$, where inverse trigonometric functions take only the principal values. Given below are two statements:
Statement I: $\cos(\alpha + \beta) > 0$
Statement II: $\cos(\alpha) < 0$
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
$\frac{1}{2} < \frac{6}{11} < \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$
$\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{2}\right) < \sin^{-1}\left(\frac{6}{11}\right) < \sin^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)$
$\frac{\pi}{6} < 3\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{6}{11}\right) < \frac{\pi}{4}$
$\frac{\pi}{2} < \alpha < \frac{3\pi}{4} \quad \therefore \cos\alpha < 0$
$0 < \frac{4}{9} < \frac{1}{2}$
$\frac{\pi}{3} < \cos^{-1}\left(\frac{4}{9}\right) < \frac{\pi}{2}$
$\pi < 3\cos^{-1}\left(\frac{4}{9}\right) < \frac{3\pi}{2}$
$\pi < \beta < \frac{3\pi}{2}$
Now $\frac{3\pi}{2} < \alpha + \beta < \frac{9\pi}{4}$
$\therefore \cos(\alpha + \beta) > 0$

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true

questions.stem:
For the function $f(x) = e^{\sin|x|} - |x|$, $x \in$ in $\mathbb{R}$ consider the following statements:
Statement I: $f$ is differentiable for all $x \in \mathbb{R}$
Statement II: $f$ is increasing in $\left(-\pi, -\frac{\pi}{2}\right)$
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution:
$f(x) = e^{\sin|x|} - |x|; \ x \in \mathbb{R}$
$f(x) = \begin{cases} e^{\sin x} - x; & x > 0 \\ e^{-\sin x} + x; & x < 0 \end{cases}$
LHD at $x = 0$
$f'(x) = e^{-\sin x}(-\cos x) + 1$
at $x = 0$
$= -1 + 1$
$= 0$
RHD at $x = 0$
$f'(x) = e^{\sin x}.\cos x - 1$
at $x = 0$
$= 1 - 1$
$= 0$
Diff at $x = 0$
Statement 1 is true
and for $x \in \left(-\pi, \frac{-\pi}{2}\right)$
$f(x) = e^{-\sin x} + x$
$f'(x) = -e^{-\sin x}\cos x + 1$
for $x \in \left(-\pi, \frac{-\pi}{2}\right) \quad \cos x < 0$
$\therefore f'(x) > 0$
$\therefore f(x)$ is increasing

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true

questions.stem: Let $\vec{a} = 4\hat{i} - \hat{j} + 3\hat{k}$, $\vec{b} = 10\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} - \hat{k}$ and a vector $\vec{c}$ such that $2(\vec{a} \times \vec{b}) + 3(\vec{b} \times \vec{c}) = \vec{0}$. If $\vec{a} \cdot \vec{c} = 15$, then $\vec{c} \cdot (\hat{i} + \hat{j} - 3\hat{k})$ is equal to :
questions.solution:
$2(\vec{a} \times \vec{b}) - 3(\vec{c} \times \vec{b}) = 0$
$(2\vec{a} - 3\vec{c}) \times \vec{b} = 0$
$|\vec{b}| = 2\vec{a} - 3\vec{c}$
$2\vec{a} - 3\vec{c} = \lambda\vec{b}$
$\vec{c} = \frac{2\vec{a} - \lambda\vec{b}}{3} \quad \ldots(1)$
$\vec{a} \cdot \vec{c} = 15$
$\left(\frac{2\vec{a} - \lambda\vec{b}}{3}\right) \cdot \vec{a} = 15$
$\frac{2|a|^{2} - \lambda\vec{b} \cdot \vec{a}}{3} = 15$
$2(26) - \lambda(40 - 2 - 3) = 45$
$\lambda = \frac{1}{5}$
$\Rightarrow \vec{c} \cdot (\hat{i} + \hat{j} - 3\hat{k}) = \frac{\left(2(4\hat{i} - \hat{j} + 3k) - \frac{1}{5}(10\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} - k) \cdot (\hat{i} + \hat{j} - 3\hat{k})\right)}{3}$
$= \frac{2(4 - 1 - 9) - \frac{1}{5}(10 + 2 + 3)}{3} = -5$

questions.stem: The value of the integral $\int_{0}^{2} \frac{\sqrt{x(x^{2} + x + 1)}}{(\sqrt{x + 1})(\sqrt{x^{4} + x^{2} + 1})}dx$ is equal to :

Let $y = y(x)$ be the solution of the differential equation .
$x\sqrt{1 - x^{2}}\,dy + \left(y\sqrt{1 - x^{2}} - x\cos^{-1}x\right)dx = 0$, $x \in (0, 1)$ $\lim_{x \to 1^{-}} y(x) = 1$. Then $y\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)$ equals :
questions.solution:
$x\sqrt{1 - x^{2}}\,dy + \left(y\sqrt{1 - x^{2}} - x\cos^{-1}x\right) \cdot dx = 0$
$\frac{dy}{dx} + \frac{y}{x} = \frac{\cos^{-1}x}{\sqrt{1 - x^{2}}}$
$P = \frac{1}{x}; Q = \frac{\cos^{-1}x}{\sqrt{1 - x^{2}}}$
I.F. $= e^{\int \frac{1}{x}dx}$
$= e^{\ln x} = x$
$y \cdot x = \int \frac{x\cos^{-1}x}{\sqrt{1 - x^{2}}}dx + c$
det $\cos^{-1}x = t$
$\frac{-1}{\sqrt{1 - x^{2}}}dx = dt$
$-\int t \cdot \cos t\,dt$
$\Rightarrow -[t\sin t + \cos t]$
$\therefore y \cdot x = -\sqrt{1 - x^{2}}\cos^{-1}x - x + C$
As $\mathop{dt}_{x \to 1^{-}} y(x) = 1$
$1.1 = -1 - \sqrt{1 - 1^{2}}\cos^{-1}1 + c$
$c = 2$
$\therefore x.y = 2 - x - \sqrt{1 - x^{2}}\cos^{-1}x$
At $x = \frac{1}{2}$
$y = 3 - \frac{\pi}{\sqrt{3}}$

questions.stem: Let $f : (1, \infty) \to \mathbb{R}$ be a function defined as $f(x) = \frac{x - 1}{x + 1}$. Let $f^{i+1}(x) = f(f^{i}(x))$, $i = 1, 2, \ldots, 25$, where $f^{1}(x) = f(x)$. If $g(x) + f^{26}(x) = 0$, $x \in (1, \infty)$, then the area of the region bounded by the curves $y = g(x)$, $2y = 2x - 3$, $y = 0$ and $x = 4$ is:
questions.solution:
$f^{2}(x) = f(f(x)) = \frac{\frac{x - 1}{x + 1} - 1}{\frac{x - 1}{x + 1} + 1} = \frac{-1}{x}$
$f^{3}(x) = f(f^{2}(x)) = f\left(\frac{-1}{x}\right) = \frac{1 + x}{1 - x}$
$f^{4}(x) = f(f^{3}(x)) = f\left(f\left(\frac{-1}{x}\right)\right) = x$
$f^{5}(x) = f(f^{4}(x)) = f(x)$
$f^{6}(x) = f(f^{5}(x)) = f(f(x)) = \frac{-1}{x}$
$f^{26}(x) = \frac{-1}{x}$
$g(x) = \frac{1}{x}$
[Figure: $y = \frac{1}{x}$, the line through $\left(\frac{3}{2}, 0\right)$ and $\left(2, \frac{1}{2}\right)$, and $x = 4$, with the region shaded]
$x - \frac{3}{2} = \frac{1}{x} \Rightarrow 2x^{2} - 3x - 2 = 0$
$\Rightarrow x = \frac{-1}{2}, 2$
Req. area $= \int_{2}^{4} \frac{1}{x}dx + \frac{1}{2} \times \frac{1}{2} \times \frac{1}{2}$
$= \frac{1}{8} + (\ln x)_{2}^{4} = \frac{1}{8} + \ln 2$

questions.stem: Let $f(x) = \begin{cases} \frac{1}{3} & , x \le \pi/2 \\ \frac{b(1 - \sin x)}{(\pi - 2x)^{2}} & x > \pi/2 \end{cases}$. If $f$ is continuous at $x = \pi/2$, then the value of $\int_{0}^{3b-6} |x^{2} + 2x - 3|\,dx$ is:
questions.solution:
$\lim_{x \to \frac{\pi}{2}^{-}} f(x) = \lim_{x \to \frac{\pi}{2}^{+}} f(x)$
LHL $= \frac{1}{3}$
RHL $= \lim_{x \to \frac{\pi}{2}^{+}} \frac{b(1 - \sin x)}{(\pi - 2x)^{2}}$
$= \lim_{h \to 0} \frac{b\left(1 - \sin\left(\frac{\pi}{2} + h\right)\right)}{\left(\pi - 2\left(\frac{\pi}{2} + h\right)\right)^{2}}$
$= \lim_{h \to 0} \frac{b(1 - \cos h)}{4h^{2}}$
$= \lim_{h \to 0} \frac{b \cdot 2 \cdot \sin^{2}\frac{h}{2}}{4h^{2}} = \frac{2b}{16} = \frac{b}{8}$
$\therefore \frac{1}{3} = \frac{b}{8} \Rightarrow b = \frac{8}{3}$
$I = \int_{0}^{2} |x^{2} + 2x - 3|\,dx$
$= \int_{0}^{1} -(x^{2} + 2x - 3)\,dx + \int_{1}^{2} (x^{2} + 2x - 3)\,dx$
$= \left[-\frac{x^{3}}{3} - \frac{2x^{2}}{2} + 3x\right]_{0}^{1} + \left[\frac{x^{3}}{3} + \frac{2x^{2}}{2} - 3x\right]_{1}^{2}$
$= \left(-\frac{1}{3} - 1 + 3\right) + \left(\frac{8}{3} + 4 - 6 - \frac{1}{3} - 1 + 3\right)$
$= \frac{5}{3} + \frac{7}{3} = 4$

questions.stem: Let $\frac{x^{2}}{f(a^{2} + 7a + 3)} + \frac{y^{2}}{f(3a + 15)} = 1$ represent an ellipse with major axis along y-axis, where $f$ is a strictly decreasing positive function on $\mathbb{R}$. If the set of all possible values of $a$ is $\mathbb{R} - [\alpha, \beta]$, then $\alpha^{2} + \beta^{2}$ is equal to:

The sum of squares of all the real solutions of the equation
$\log_{(x+1)}(2x^{2} + 5x + 3) = 4 - \log_{(2x+3)}(x^{2} + 2x + 1)$ is equal to ________.
If $\int_{\pi/4}^{3\pi/4} \left(\cot\left(x - \frac{\pi}{3}\right)\cot\left(x + \frac{\pi}{3}\right) + 1\right)dx = \alpha\log_{e}(\sqrt{3} - 1)$, then $9\alpha^{2}$ is equal to ________.
questions.solution:
$\int_{\pi/6}^{\pi/4} \left(\left(\cot\left(x - \frac{\pi}{3}\right)\cot\left(x + \frac{\pi}{3}\right) + 1\right)\right)dx$
using $\cot(A - B) = \frac{\cot B\cot A + 1}{\cot B - \cot A}$
$\Rightarrow \int_{\pi/6}^{\pi/4} -\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\left[\cot\left(x - \frac{\pi}{3}\right) - \cot\left(x + \frac{\pi}{3}\right)\right]dx$
$\Rightarrow \frac{-1}{\sqrt{3}}\left[\ln\left|\frac{\sin\left(x - \frac{\pi}{3}\right)}{\sin\left(x + \frac{\pi}{3}\right)}\right|\right]_{\frac{\pi}{6}}^{\frac{\pi}{4}}$
$= \frac{-1}{\sqrt{3}}\left[\ln\left|\left(\frac{\sin 15^\circ}{\sin 75^\circ}\right)\right| - \ln\left|\frac{\sin 30^\circ}{\sin 90^\circ}\right|\right]$
$= \frac{-1}{\sqrt{3}}\left[\ln(\tan 15^\circ) - \ln\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)\right]$
$= \frac{-1}{\sqrt{3}}\left[\ln(2 - \sqrt{3}) + \ln 2\right]$
$\Rightarrow \frac{-1}{\sqrt{3}}\ln(4 - 2\sqrt{3}) = \frac{-2}{\sqrt{3}}\ln(\sqrt{3} - 1)$
$\therefore \alpha = \frac{-2}{\sqrt{3}} \therefore 9\alpha^{2} = 12$

questions.stem:
Let a line $L_1$ pass through the origin and be perpendicular to the lines
$L_2 : \vec{r} = (3 + t)\hat{i} + (2t - 1)\hat{j} + (2t + 4)\hat{k}$ and
$L_3 : \vec{r} = (3 + 2s)\hat{i} + (3 + 2s)\hat{j} + (2 + s)\hat{k}$, $t, s \in \mathbb{R}$.
If $(a, b, c)$, $a \in \mathbb{Z}$, is the point on $L_3$ at a distance of $\sqrt{17}$ from the point of intersection of $L_1$ and $L_2$, then $(a + b + c)^{2}$ is equal to ________.
questions.solution:
Direction of line $L_1 = \vec{v}_2 \times \vec{v}_3$
$= \begin{vmatrix} i & j & k \\ 1 & 2 & 2 \\ 2 & 2 & 1 \end{vmatrix} = -2i + 3j - 2k$
$\therefore L_1 = \vec{0} + \lambda(-2i + 3j - 2k)$
Now point of intersec line of $L_2$ and $L_3$
$-2\lambda = 3 + t, \quad \ldots(1)$
$3\lambda = 2t - 1$ and $\quad \ldots(2)$
$-2\lambda = 2t + 4 \quad \ldots(3)$
from (1) and (3)
$3 + t = 2t + 4$
$t = -1$
$-2\lambda = 2$
$\lambda = -1$
$\therefore$ Point of intersection $(2, -3, 2)$
The point $(a, b, c)$ lies on $L_3$ it has the form $(3 + 2s, 3 + 2s, 2 + s)$
Dist from $(2, -3, 2)$ from it $\sqrt{17}$
$\therefore (3 + 2s - 2)^{2} + (3 + 2s + 3)^{2} + (2 + s - 2)^{2} = 17$
$9s^{2} + 28s + 20 = 0$
$s = -10/9, -2$
as $a, b, c \in \mathbb{Z}$
$\therefore s = -2$
$a = -1$
$b = -1$
$c = 0$
$(a + b + c)^{2} = 4$

questions.stem: Consider the circle $C : x^{2} + y^{2} - 6x - 8y - 11 = 0$. Let a variable chord $AB$ of the circle $C$ subtend a right angle at the origin. If the locus of the foot of the perpendicular drawn from the origin on the chord $AB$ is the circle $x^{2} + y^{2} - \alpha x - \beta y - \gamma = 0$, then $\alpha + \beta + 2\gamma$ is equal to ________.
questions.solution:
Equation of $AB$
[Figure: chord $AB$ of the circle subtending $90^\circ$ at $O(0, 0)$, foot of perpendicular $P(h, k)$, $m_{AB} = -\frac{h}{k}$, $m_{OP} = \frac{k}{h}$]
$y - k = -\frac{h}{k}(x - h)$
$hx + ky = h^{2} + k^{2}$
H.F. : $\frac{hx + ky}{h^{2} + k^{2}} = 1$
Now, $x^{2} + y^{2} - (6x + 8y)\left(\frac{hx + ky}{h^{2} + k^{2}}\right) - 11\left(\frac{hx + ky}{h^{2} + k^{2}}\right)^{2} = 0$
Now coeff of $x^{2}$ + coeff of $y^{2} = 0$
$2 - \frac{6h + 8k}{h^{2} + k^{2}} - \frac{11}{h^{2} + k^{2}} = 0$
$2h^{2} + 2k^{2} - 6h - 8k - 11 = 0$
$x^{2} + y^{2} - 3x - 4y - 55 = 0$
$\alpha + \beta + 2\gamma = 3 + 4 + 11$
$= 18$

questions.stem:
Let $f$ be a polynomial function such that
$\log_{2}(f(x)) = \left(\log_{2}\left(2 + \frac{2}{3} + \frac{2}{9} + \ldots\ldots \infty\right)\right) \cdot \log_{3}\left(1 + \frac{f(x)}{f(1/x)}\right)$, $x > 0$ and $f(6) = 37$. Then $\sum_{n=1}^{10} f(n)$ is equal to ________.
questions.solution:
$S = 2 + \frac{2}{3} + \frac{2}{9} + \cdots$
$= \frac{2}{1 - 1/3} = 3$
$\log_{2}(f'(x)) = \log_{2}3.\log_{3}\left(1 + \frac{f(x)}{f\left(\frac{1}{x}\right)}\right)$
$= \log_{2}\left(1 + \frac{f(x)}{f\left(\frac{1}{x}\right)}\right)$
$\Rightarrow f(x) + f\left(\frac{1}{x}\right) = f(x) \cdot f\left(\frac{1}{x}\right)$
$\therefore f(x) = 1 + x^{n}$ and $f(6) = 37$
$\therefore n = 2$
$\therefore f(x) = 1 + x^{2}$
Now $\sum_{n=1}^{10} f(n)$
$\sum_{n=1}^{10} 1 + n^{2}$
$\Rightarrow 10 + \frac{10 \times 11 \times 21}{6} \Rightarrow 395$
